transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-18
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes (recorded)
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Luis Ortega (Redwood PM); Ethan Cole (SilverWillow CTO), Priya Nair (Head of Platform), Samir Bhatt (Infra), Olivia Reed (Security)
---
Summary:
Quick partner intro / discovery focused on SilverWillow's plan to onboard a SaaS product onto Redwood's hosted/dedicated offering with hybrid VPC connectivity. Primary concerns: data residency, predictable latency for inference, and procurement timeline for reserved capacity.
Topics: Hosted vs Dedicated tradeoffs, VPC/private deployment options, KV cache behaviour for high-QPS micro-calls, benchmarks and pilot framing, security/compliance checklist.
---
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for doing this. um, we'll go quick — intro on our side then we'll dive into your architecture and constraints. Maya's gonna cover the technical bits.
[00:18] Ethan (SilverWillow): thanks, Jordan. quick note, we're spread across us-west and eu-central data centers. our customers care about sub-75ms tail latency for short prompts, and we've got compliance needs for logs and PII.
[00:35] Maya (Redwood SE): got it. just to set expectations: we support hosted, dedicated reserved pools, and private VPC/on-prem. in practice folks start hosted to iterate then move to dedicated for predictable throughput, or private if there's strict network or residency controls.
[00:52] Priya (SilverWillow): timeline wise we're aiming for a beta in Q3, procurement signoff by end of july. curious on how you handle routing between regions and if we can pin model versions.
[01:10] Jordan: yep you can pin model versions, and routing is policy-driven — you can prefer latency region and fall back to compatible quantized variants if capacity's constrained.
[01:25] Samir (SilverWillow): quick question about KV cache — we do lots of short prompt completions with context, is that helpful? we've heard kv cache can reduce token cost but not sure about warmup jitter.
[01:40] Maya: KV cache helps a lot for prefix-heavy workloads, reduces repeated compute — though warm cache hit rates depend on request similarity and session affinity. we also do prefix caching and can suggest batching windows. some customers call it K-V cash or KV.. uh, K-V cache — transcription sometimes shows it weirdly.
[02:05] Olivia (SilverWillow): security — we need SOC2 type II, ISO27001 and enterprise SSO (SAML/Okta). also, encryption keys managed by us via KMS/HSM — can you support customer-managed keys for private?
[02:25] Jordan: yes for Private we support KMS integrations and customer-managed keys. for Hosted we offer envelope encryption; dedicated can be configured to use your KMS depending on contract. we'll send certs and the compliance pack.
[02:40] Ethan: and data retention — logs/requests — we need to ensure raw request logs aren't retained longer than 30 days and that they can be disabled for PII-sensitive routes.
[02:55] Maya: we have per-route retention controls and token-level redaction options. we also have an audit log with RBAC. we'll attach the doc.
[03:10] Jordan: can I ask about current infra — what are you running inference on today?
[03:18] Priya: currently a mix — we self-host some lightweight embedding jobs on k8s with inference containers, and for heavy gen we're evaluating cloud providers. procurement wants an apples-to-apples of cost per 1m tokens for our typical mix.
[03:36] Luis (Redwood): when you say typical mix, can you send a token distribution? sequence lengths? we can run a small benchmark and show throughput and tail latency across model variants.
[03:50] Priya: yes, we'll share a sample workload and QPS profile, aim is mostly 20-200 QPS spikes during peak.
[04:06] Samir: important — we need predictable p95 under 90ms for short (<=128 tokens) completions. if you have any published perf profiles that map to hardware types that'd help procurement.
[04:22] Maya: we have model profiles for a few open models and internal benchmarks across common GPUs. for Dedicated we commit latency SLOs on pre-agreed configs. we can share a trimmed matrix that maps model variant, sequence length and GPU instance type to p50/p95 numbers.
[04:40] Ethan: on-network connectivity, we have strict controls — would prefer VPC peering to hosted or a Private deployment. what's the difference in effort to go from Hosted to Private?
[04:55] Jordan: Hosted is the fastest, very low onboarding time. Private involves setting up a customer control plane and connectivity — options: VPC peering with private endpoints, or a full on-prem bundle. the effort depends on VPC topology, cross-account peering, and whether you need encryption at rest with your KMS. typically 2-6 weeks for Private with standard peering, longer if air-gapped.
[05:20] Priya: procurement will push for Dedicated first — reserved capacity with guaranteed throughput — can you explain burst capacity and autoscaling behavior for Dedicated?
[05:35] Maya: Dedicated pools are reserved GPUs for your tenant, autoscaling policies allow queued bursts to utilize spare capacity up to X; we can define bursting caps in the contract. for latency-sensitive workloads we recommend configuring lower batch windows and higher concurrency for the workers.
[05:55] Jordan: and cost-wise, Dedicated affects unit economics but buys predictability. our Optimize toolkit can suggest quantizations and batching params to hit a target p95 or cost per token.
[06:10] Ethan: any limitations on model size with Dedicated/private? like 70b vs 13b and quantization tradeoffs?
[06:22] Maya: we support a range; larger models will need more GPU memory or sharded runtimes. quantization can reduce memory but sometimes impacts output quality; we can run evals to measure quality delta per model/quant config.
[06:40] Samir: I want to call out network egress costs — do you have routing that keeps inference regional to avoid cross-region egress?
[06:52] Luis: yes routing policies let you prefer regional pools. we can also set fallbacks to a cheaper region if desired, but you'd get a notice and configurable policies.
[07:10] [Jordan shares a quick screen note] Jordan: i'll summarize proposed next steps, then Maya will propose an initial pilot shape.
[07:20] Maya: Pilot thought: 2-week benchmark window — we'll run your sample workload against hosted and a dedicated reserved pool equivalent. 2-hour dedicated benchmark slot for p95 tail latency tests during your peak QPS window. We'll provide configs (batching, concurrency, cache) and a suggested kv/prefix caching policy.
[07:40] Priya: that sounds good. what about telemetry — we need token-level cost breakdowns, traces and model-level metrics.
[07:52] Maya: Console exposes per-route token costs, latency histograms, and trace hooks. we can keep the retention time to match your compliance needs.
[08:05] Olivia: OS account & access — we need RBAC scoped to team and audit logs with SSO. also, do you support SCIM for provisioning?
[08:18] Jordan: yes SSO via SAML/Okta and SCIM for user provisioning are supported for enterprise plans. audit logs are available with configurable retention.
[08:30] Samir: procurement question — are there minimum contract lengths for Dedicated? we prefer 6 months or 1 year.
[08:42] Jordan: Dedicated typically has a 12-month reservation for the best rates but we can discuss 6-month pilot rates and convert to annual reserved as you scale.
[08:55] Ethan: can you outline a red-team-style security review window? security will run penetration and compliance tests before procurement closes.
[09:06] Jordan: absolutely — we provide a security checklist, SOC2 reports, and can coordinate an NDA and PoV approval path. we usually book a 2-week window for security review in parallel with technical pilot.
[09:20] Priya: question about fallbacks — if Dedicated pool is saturated do you spill to hosted? what's data flow and policy?
[09:32] Maya: yes you can configure automatic fallback: either to a compatible quantized variant in another Dedicated pool or to Hosted. data routing and logs follow the same retention policies; we log fallbacks and can notify ops.
[09:48] Samir: in terms of integration, we run k8s and want to keep inference clients in our service mesh. what's the recommended pattern for low-latency calls? sidecar vs direct SDK?
[10:00] Maya: recommended is using a lightweight inference client or sidecar that maintains session affinity and connection pooling. SDKs are available in go/python/node; sidecar helps with retries and batching locally.
[10:16] Jordan: ok, jumping ahead to procurement checklist: we'll send pricing tiers (hosted, dedicated commit levels, private), compliance docs, a network appendix for VPC peering, and a pilot plan.
[10:30] Ethan: great. on the pilot, will you be able to include example configs for batching windows and quantization?
[10:40] Maya: yes we'll include tuned examples based on your sample workload. we'll also suggest an Optimize profile with quantization candidates and expected cost delta.
[10:55] Priya: for the benchmark do you need service account credentials or sample synthetic traffic?
[11:05] Maya: for hosted benchmarking we can do synthetic from our side but for dedicated/private we prefer a short run with your sample traces or synthetic replay to match QPS and token distributions. we'll provide a runbook for data redaction if there are PII concerns.
[11:25] Olivia: can we get the compliance pack and network appendix by eod? procurement will want to start reviewing Monday.
[11:33] Jordan: we'll send the compliance pack and network appendix tomorrow morning PST.
[11:40] [brief cross-talk about calendars, scheduling]
[11:55] Ethan: any blockers we haven't covered?
[12:02] Samir: just one — can we see cost projections including egress and storage for logs? that tends to surprise folks.
[12:12] Luis: we'll include egress estimates in the pricing worksheet and show a scenario with your sample workload.
[12:22] Jordan: quick recap: Redwood to send pricing worksheet, compliance pack + SOC2/ISO certs, proposed pilot plan and runbook, schedule 1-hr technical deep dive next week. SilverWillow to share sample token distributions, network diagrams, and list of stakeholders for security review.
[12:40] Priya: perfect. we'll aim to send artifacts by friday (2027-05-21).
[12:45] Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs.
[12:50] End of recording.
